free_tier.stated: Turbo free tier: 105 KiB per data item, 10 MiB over the lifetime of a wallet AND 10 MiB over the lifetime of an IP range. Larger files are billed.

egress.terms: Arweave reads are effectively unmetered through gateways (arweave.net, ar.io gateways). Genuinely free egress, which is why this would otherwise be interesting. But there is nothing to serve.

record.tooling: ario-deploy CLI, Turbo SDK (@ardriveapp/turbo-sdk), ar.io SDK; arbundles/Irys for direct bundling.
record.chaining: Actively defeated by design: the IP-range meter means the entire free allowance for a datacenter is shared. 'ario-deploy can check the wallet's allowance... It cannot check the IP range, so a deploy can pass the credit check and still be refused at upload time with HTTP 402 when other people on the same network have used the range's allowance.'
record.limits_note: 105 KiB/file; 10 MiB/wallet lifetime; 10 MiB/IP-range lifetime; HTTP 402 past that.
record.reliability_note: The IP-range metering is the anti-farming mechanism, and it works: this is the one design in the class that explicitly anticipates the 'unlimited wallets' move. Confirms the prior agent's finding, with the mechanism spelled out (dual metering, wallet + range, 402 on the range).

record.notes: Turbo free tier: 105 KiB per data item, 10 MiB over the lifetime of a wallet AND 10 MiB over the lifetime of an IP range. Larger files are billed.

record.provider: Arweave via Turbo / ar.io free tier

free_tier.stated: Free tier: 105 KiB per data item, and only 10 MiB over the lifetime of a wallet AND 10 MiB over the lifetime of an IP range. Anything larger is billed in Turbo credits.

retention.stated: | Data is permanent once paid, but the free path is metered by IP range so a datacenter host fails at upload time with 402 regardless of wallet balance.

egress.terms: Free and permanent by design (Arweave pays storage endowment up front; gateways serve reads without metering).

record.chaining: The 10 MiB wallet cap is the point: unlimited wallets x 10 MiB = still trivial, and the per-IP-range cap blocks the obvious Sybil route from one host. 20 TiB would need ~2 million wallets x 10 MiB.
record.limits_note: 105 KiB/file; 10 MiB/wallet; 10 MiB/IP-range; HTTP 402 over the cap; wallet signing required per item.
